title: Combat Phase & Mission Evaluation
subtitle: No attacks and no blockers: combat in Mythos is a clash of Power over every mission.
summary: The ninjas you commit during the Action phase clash in Mission evaluation. Learn how Power is counted, why missions resolve from D to A, who wins ties, and how the points add up.

steps.title: Combat is a Power clash
steps.body: Mythos has no attack step and nothing to block. Combat happens on the missions: during the [[Action phase]] you commit ninjas to missions, and in [[Mission evaluation]] each mission becomes a clash of total Power. The side with more Power wins it. Every card you play is a move in up to four tug-of-wars running at the same time.

steps.title: Counting Power
steps.body: A face-up character's Power is its printed Power, plus its [[Power tokens]], plus any boosts from active effects such as Gaara's [[continuous]] bonus. A [[hidden]] character counts as **0**, plus any tokens it carries. Add up every character on your side of a mission to get your total. This hidden Shikamaru holds 1 token, so he adds 1 Power.
bullets: Your total: everything on your side of that mission

steps.title: Score D, then C, B, A
steps.body: Missions resolve one at a time, in [[rank]] order: the D-rank mission first, then C, B and A. Each mission's rank was fixed by the Round it entered play. Order matters when [[SCORE]] effects are involved, because each one resolves as soon as its mission is won, before the next mission is checked.

steps.title: Ties and empty sides
steps.body: The higher total wins. If both sides are level, the [[Edge token]] holder wins the mission. There is also a floor: you need **at least 1 Power** to win. If neither side has any Power on a mission, nobody scores it. Even the Edge can't win a mission with 0 Power, and a hidden card without tokens doesn't count toward that floor.

callout.text: Most Power wins. Tie: the Edge holder wins. 0 Power: you can't win.

steps.title: Points: base plus rank
steps.body: The winner gains the mission's printed base points plus its rank bonus: **+1** for D, **+2** for C, **+3** for B, **+4** for A. Then they activate any [[SCORE]] effects on the mission and on their own characters assigned to it. A 2-point mission that arrived in Round 3 is B-rank, so winning it is worth 2 + 3 = **5** [[Mission points]].

steps.title: Every mission, every Round
steps.body: Missions stay in play after they're scored, and so do your characters. **Every** mission in play is evaluated every Round: one in Round 1, two in Round 2, and all four in Round 4. The D-rank mission can be won four times, so early control keeps paying, while the A-rank mission is the biggest single prize of the game.

callout.text: You score as many missions as the current Round number: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10 mission wins are up for grabs in a game.

steps.title: Clean-up in the End phase
steps.body: After scoring, the [[End phase]] clears the board's extras: both players discard leftover Chakra and **all Power tokens** are removed. Characters stay where they are, so next Round every ninja starts again from its printed Power. After Round 4, the player with the most [[Mission points]] wins, and a tied score goes to the Edge holder.

widget.title: Mission Evaluator
widget.brief: Four missions, four clashes. Predict who wins each one, counting tokens, hidden cards and the [[Edge token]], then run [[Mission evaluation]] from D to A and watch the points land.

quiz.prompt: Both players have 4 Power on the C-rank mission, and your opponent holds the Edge token. Who wins it?
choices: You, because you played there first
Your opponent, because the Edge holder wins ties
quiz.explanation: Ties in [[Mission evaluation]] go to the [[Edge token]] holder, as long as they have at least 1 Power there.

quiz.prompt: You win a mission with 2 base points that entered play in Round 3. How many Mission points do you gain?
quiz.explanation: Round 3 makes it a B-rank mission, worth its base points + 3. That's 2 + 3 = **5** [[Mission points]].

quiz.prompt: Your only character on a mission is a hidden card with 1 Power token. Your opponent has nothing there. What happens?
choices: Nobody wins; hidden cards always have 0 Power
You win: a hidden card counts as 0 plus its tokens, so you have 1 Power
Your opponent wins with the Edge
The hidden card is revealed for free
quiz.explanation: [[hidden|Hidden]] characters have 0 printed Power but keep their [[Power tokens]]. 1 Power beats 0, and meets the 1-Power minimum.
